title: Content Production Workflow
summary: Plan, evaluate, publish, and verify one bounded existing-site content artifact while preserving business context, factual limits, approval, freshness, and lifecycle ownership.

required_inputs.description: The site, topic, audience need, or business outcome that one bounded content artifact must support.

scope.guidance: Maintain one bounded context record covering audience, business goal, page role, conversion path, market, editorial constraints, approval ownership, and lifecycle constraints.

completion_without.limitation: The method cannot support an outline, draft evaluation, approval, or lifecycle decision without sufficient business and editorial context.

evidence_plan.fallback: Return an incomplete handoff naming the unresolved context and responsible owner.

scope.guidance: Read the published page and no more than five existing pages needed to resolve taxonomy, overlap, preservation, or internal-link questions.

completion_without.limitation: The method cannot confirm the published artifact or its relationship to relevant existing pages without client-observed page content.

evidence_plan.fallback: Return an incomplete handoff and identify the exact page evidence the client must supply.

scope.guidance: Expand no more than fifty candidate queries when seed expansion can materially change the outline.

evidence_plan.condition: Use expansion only when supplied context does not already identify the material audience questions and candidate subtopics.

completion_without.limitation: The outline is limited to user and client evidence and cannot claim that omitted subtopics were tested through server expansion.

evidence_plan.fallback: Use the supported supplied context, label topic discovery as limited, and lower confidence where the missing expansion matters.

scope.guidance: Measure only candidates whose metrics can change subtopic selection, emphasis, or priority.

evidence_plan.condition: Use metrics only when qualitative fit and current intent evidence cannot distinguish material candidate subtopics.

completion_without.limitation: Subtopic priority remains qualitative and must not imply measured demand.

evidence_plan.fallback: Prioritize with supported audience, business, and intent evidence and record that quantitative comparison was unavailable.

scope.guidance: Inspect no more than three representative current result sets when intent, page type, or result format can change the outline.

evidence_plan.condition: Use current result evidence only when the selected focus or page role remains materially ambiguous.

completion_without.limitation: The handoff cannot claim that current result patterns or page-type expectations were verified.

evidence_plan.fallback: Preserve the ambiguity as a constraint and avoid unsupported intent or page-type claims.

scope.guidance: Maintain one canonical Markdown, HTML, or text document with explicit metadata provenance and a stable client-owned identity.

completion_without.limitation: The method cannot analyze, approve, publish, or verify content without one canonical client-owned document.

evidence_plan.fallback: Return an incomplete handoff and request a canonical document from the responsible content capability.

scope.guidance: Evaluate the canonical document once against the supported focus and preserve structural reliability and input limitations.

completion_without.limitation: The method cannot claim that the supplied document received its required focus-specific content review.

evidence_plan.fallback: Return an incomplete handoff without presenting the document as publication-ready.

scope.guidance: Evaluate the canonical document once when a people-first quality regression could change approval or revision.

evidence_plan.condition: Use helpfulness analysis only when the draft, intended audience, or an SEO-motivated edit raises a material people-first quality question.

completion_without.limitation: The handoff cannot claim that model-based helpfulness concerns were evaluated.

evidence_plan.fallback: Use human editorial review, record the unavailable check, and do not infer search-engine classifier behavior.

scope.guidance: Evaluate the canonical document once when textual complexity could change audience fit or expose a regression.

evidence_plan.condition: Use readability analysis only when audience fit or a proposed edit creates a material complexity question.

completion_without.limitation: The handoff cannot claim that textual complexity was measured.

evidence_plan.fallback: Use human editorial review, record the unavailable measurement, and do not claim comprehension.

scope.guidance: Maintain one bounded verification record for material factual claims, including an explicit empty set when none require external verification.

completion_without.limitation: Content-analysis scores cannot establish whether material factual claims are accurate.

evidence_plan.fallback: Return an incomplete handoff identifying the unverified material claims and the evidence owner required to continue.

scope.guidance: Publish the approved canonical artifact through one independently authorized client-owned surface and return its intended public URL.

completion_without.limitation: The end-to-end method cannot complete without explicit approval and client-owned publication evidence.

evidence_plan.fallback: Return an incomplete publication handoff without implying that the server can mutate a CMS.

scope.guidance: Inspect current metadata and static page declarations for the one published URL.

completion_without.limitation: The method cannot verify the published page's current declared identity and structure.

evidence_plan.fallback: Return an incomplete handoff with the live metadata verification still required.

scope.guidance: Inspect current blocking transport and technical signals for the one published URL.

completion_without.limitation: The method cannot rule out an immediate observable publication blocker.

evidence_plan.fallback: Return an incomplete handoff with the live technical verification still required.

steps.instruction: Confirm the audience, business goal, page role, conversion path, market, editorial and factual constraints, known site context, approval owner, and lifecycle constraints before paid research.
Inspect current runtime authorization and cost for the required path and only those conditional research or analysis steps that can change a decision.
Use supplied site evidence and one bounded research burst before outlining only when candidate subtopics, intent, page type, or priority can materially change.
Have the client prepare an outline that links material sections, proof needs, and internal-link needs to supported context or evidence, then obtain the required approval.

Have a separate client content capability create and edit one canonical document; prefer explicit title and meta-description provenance and keep publishing-only instructions outside analyzed body content.
Run the required focus-specific review and only the conditional quality checks whose result can change revision or approval; do not maximize scores blindly.
Verify material factual claims through appropriate public, first-party, or user-supplied evidence independently of content-analysis scores.

Record the canonical artifact identity, evidence-backed requirements, preservation and prohibition constraints, missing inputs, intended URL, acceptance criteria, and verification plan without embedding finished content.
Obtain the required human or client approval for the exact canonical artifact and publication target.
Route publication to an independently authorized client-owned capability; the recipe does not grant CMS authority or perform mutation.
Read the published page and inspect current metadata and blocking technical signals, requesting fresh evidence only when immediate verification justifies the current full quote.
For time-limited content, record the review trigger and decision owner without inferring retain, update, unpublish, noindex, or redirect.
Return the evidence-linked implementation handoff with publication verification, limitations, completion state, and remaining lifecycle ownership.

evidence_requirements: Every outline and publication requirement links to user, client, or server evidence or is labeled as an unresolved constraint.
Generated variants, third-party estimates, content-analysis scores, and client-supplied snapshots retain their distinct provenance and limitations.
Material factual claims have separate verification evidence or an explicit blocking record; content-analysis scores never satisfy factual verification.
Publication and live verification are client and server evidence respectively; a staged snapshot cannot establish production equivalence.
The canonical page body remains a client-owned artifact and is not embedded in the validated handoff.
stop_conditions: Stop or narrow before paid research when the audience, market, page role, factual constraints, or approval ownership is materially ambiguous.
Stop before a paid step when current authorization or budget is insufficient for the selected bounded evidence path.
Stop publication when the canonical document, factual verification, or required approval is incomplete.
Return an incomplete handoff when the published page or required live verification evidence cannot be obtained.
completion_criteria: The business and editorial context, research bounds, approved outline, and canonical artifact identity are recorded.
Required and selected conditional analyses are evidence-linked, and score conflicts or input limitations are explicit.
Material factual claims are separately verified or the result stops incomplete.
Approval, client-owned publication, live page reading, metadata, and technical verification are recorded.
The handoff is self-contained, contains no finished page body, and identifies lifecycle ownership and any remaining checks.

bounds.sample_guidance: Produce one approved canonical artifact and inspect only the research, comparison pages, and quality signals that can change its structure, publication decision, or verification.
